record.original_question: Is every 4-connected graph that embeds in the torus Hamiltonian?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6 Is every 4-connected toroidal graph Hamiltonian?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G be a finite simple graph that admits a cellular embedding in the torus (the orientable closed surface of genus 1). Assume G is 4-connected, meaning |V(G)| ≥ 5 and G − S is connected for every set S ⊆ V(G) with |S| ≤ 3. Must G contain a Hamilton cycle, i.e., a cycle passing through every vertex of G exactly once?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Grünbaum and Nash-Williams) that every 4-connected toroidal graph is Hamiltonian remains open. Partial results are known: Thomas and Yu proved that every 5-connected toroidal graph has a Hamilton cycle, and every 4-connected toroidal graph is known to contain a Hamilton path. The problem is listed as open on the Open Problem Garden.
